title: Map the streets missing from a tree inventory
task: Give a neighborhood group a map of recorded trees and a list of places where the city’s inventory may need another look.
prompt: Open the city tree inventory for [area]. Plot entries with usable coordinates, count missing locations by neighborhood, and give me five stretches to check on foot. Label empty patches as gaps in the records.
check: Open three plotted records against the original rows. Compare a supposedly empty street with a street-level photograph before calling it treeless.
inputs: A city tree inventory with coordinates and a neighborhood boundary

title: Find the line item behind a scanned budget total
task: Recover a sortable table from a scanned public budget with a page reference for every amount.
prompt: Take the [department] tables in this PDF. Extract each line under its printed year and unit, carry headers across page breaks, then add each section and flag differences from the printed subtotal.
check: Check the last row before a page break, the first row after it, and every subtotal that failed to reconcile against the scan.
inputs: A public budget PDF with scanned tables
sourceLabel: PDF extraction demo and discussion on Hacker News

title: Build a quote index you can play back
task: Find exactly where a speaker committed to a deadline in a long public hearing.
prompt: Search this hearing recording for statements about [promise]. Return the time, speaker, short quotation and ten seconds of context on either side. Include the moment anyone amended the date or qualified the promise.
check: Play every proposed clip before quoting it. Resolve any speaker the transcript identifies only by a number.
inputs: A public hearing recording and the promise you want to check

title: Catch a council agenda change before the vote
task: Get a dated record when a public meeting packet gains an item, changes wording or moves a vote.
prompt: Compare the latest [council] packet against the saved version for the same meeting. Report changed agenda text, item number and links to both versions. Ignore file timestamps and page-number shifts.
check: Open the two official packets at the cited items. Confirm an amendment really changed the proposal before alerting anyone.
inputs: Public agenda page, previous packet and a read-only web connection

title: Trace a lobbying lead back to its filings
task: Build a reporting lead that a colleague can follow from a public statement to the underlying disclosures.
prompt: Start with [policy topic] and [date range]. Search lobbying disclosures and congressional press releases. Join matching organizations and dates, retain filing IDs, and give me the strongest lead plus an alternative explanation.
check: Inspect the original filing and release. Confirm the legal entity, reporting period and issue code before approaching a source.
inputs: Public lobbying records, press releases and a narrow policy question
sourceLabel: Emma Bingham and Ian Clester’s GAIN newsroom project

title: Untangle company names in public records
task: Create a traceable map of companies that appear under different names across a public document collection.
prompt: Read these public filings. For each company alias, show the page that connects the two names, any dates and the relationship stated. Put possible name matches in a separate review list.
check: Check every proposed merger of two names against an identifier or an explicit statement in the original document.
inputs: Public filings suitable for the agent’s data environment

title: Hear the minority view in consultation responses
task: Turn free-text feedback into an issue register that keeps uncommon objections visible.
prompt: Read the de-identified responses to [proposal]. Tag each with a theme and response ID. Count distinct responses per theme, show short examples, and give concerns raised by just one or two people their own section.
check: Read a random set of tagged answers plus every rare objection. Confirm counts refer to responses and explain where one response covers two topics.
inputs: A question and a de-identified export of consultation responses
sourceLabel: UK government’s transparency record for Consult

title: Choose which grants your team can finish
task: Fit a realistic grant shortlist into a calendar with limited writing time.
prompt: Here are our project, deadlines and available writing hours. Read each funder’s rules, exclude ineligible calls with the exact clause, and suggest two combinations we could complete. Show the first deadline each combination puts at risk.
check: Open every shortlisted funder’s guidelines and confirm the date, geography and applicant type. Replace estimated writing time with your team’s own figures.
inputs: Funder links, project outline and available hours

title: Find the holes in a grant application
task: See which questions lack evidence or attachments before the final writing day.
prompt: Match each requirement in this funding call to our approved program materials. Give me the page or file supporting each answer, the word limit and a short list of gaps to assign. Leave unsupported outcomes blank.
check: Count the requirements against the original call, including attachments and budget notes. Have the program owner confirm each outcome number.
inputs: Funding call, approved proposals, current budget and outcome report

title: Get a volunteer ready for their first shift
task: Create a role-specific first-shift packet from the organization’s actual policies and training materials.
prompt: Build a one-page first-shift guide for [volunteer role]. Walk from arrival to handover, link each required training, and say who to call when a task falls outside the role. Flag any missing contact or conflicting instruction.
check: A returning volunteer follows the guide using only its links. Ask the coordinator to resolve conflicting policies before sharing.
inputs: Role description, current handbook, training links and coordinator contacts

title: Put competing vendor quotes on the same basis
task: Find the true comparable cost when suppliers quote different pack sizes, service periods or delivery fees.
prompt: Build a comparison sheet for [quantity and term]. Extract unit size, tax treatment, delivery, included support and exclusions for each offer. Show the arithmetic and draft one clarification per unresolved difference.
check: Trace the cheapest total to its quoted units and fees. Keep any offer with an unknown mandatory charge out of the final ranking.
inputs: Two or more quotes you may share and the actual order specification

title: Find the assumption that makes a market estimate swing
task: Build a market estimate with a workbook you can change during a planning meeting.
prompt: For [product, buyer and region], count plausible buyers from named sources and estimate annual spend from supplied prices. Give me low and high cases, then show which single input changes the estimate most.
check: Trace one buyer-count figure to its source and change one price in the sheet. The totals and chart should recalculate together.
inputs: A defined buyer, geographic boundary, research links and price assumptions

title: Trace a board-slide number to the annual filing
task: Make a citation card for a financial figure before it appears in a presentation.
prompt: Find [metric] in [company]’s annual filing for [fiscal year]. Give the table heading, reporting period, unit and page. If a later filing restates it, show both values with their dates and explain the difference using the note.
check: Recalculate the value from the cited table when possible. Check the fiscal year and whether the units are dollars, thousands or millions.
inputs: Company, fiscal year, metric and public annual filings

title: Check translated instructions before they go to print
task: Produce a bilingual review sheet that lets a fluent editor catch changes in meaning.
prompt: Translate this instruction sheet for [audience] using the approved terms. Keep numbering, measurements and form-field names aligned with the original. Flag phrases with two plausible meanings and explain the choice beside each.
check: Have a fluent reviewer check the flagged lines, amounts, dates and required actions against the original before publication.
inputs: Approved source copy, target locale and a terminology list
sourceLabel: Lokalise translation workflow and customer interview

title: Screen a reading pile without losing borderline studies
task: Give a reviewer a shorter queue with a documented reason for every proposed exclusion.
prompt: Apply these inclusion criteria to the attached abstracts. Produce include, exclude and full-text-needed queues. Quote the sentence supporting each decision and retain the original citation when the abstract gives too little detail.
check: Manually check all borderline cases and a random sample of exclusions. Test that a known qualifying paper survives the screen.
inputs: Citation export, abstracts and written inclusion criteria

title: Catch a measurement mismatch before pooling studies
task: Build an evidence table that reveals when apparently comparable results measure different things.
prompt: Extract outcome definition, measurement scale, follow-up time, group size and result from each paper on [question]. Link each cell to its source page. Group only results with a common definition and time point.
check: Verify one complete row and all apparent outliers in the papers. Have a subject expert decide whether any proposed group can be combined.
inputs: Full-text papers and one precisely defined outcome

title: Check what a trial originally planned to measure
task: Spot changes between a registered study plan and the paper that reported its results.
prompt: Find the registry ID for each paper and retrieve the registered primary outcome, sample and observation window. Compare the dated registry entry with the published methods. Flag missing outcomes and record amendment dates.
check: Match the registry ID, study population and registration version yourself. Record any unexplained amendment as a question for the authors.
inputs: Public trial papers, registry identifiers or author and study names

title: Find the closest earlier test of a research idea
task: Prepare a short list of the experiments a proposal must distinguish itself from.
prompt: Look for studies testing [idea] in [population or setting]. Search neighboring terminology and cited references. For the three closest studies, compare the intervention, outcome and design; show exactly what my proposed test would add.
check: Read the methods of the closest match. Record the searches tried and leave the question open if key full texts could not be checked.
inputs: A proposed research question, scope and related terms
sourceLabel: FutureHouse demonstration of literature and novelty searches

title: Find a weakness in your paper before peer review
task: Receive a short list of actionable objections to an unpublished draft you are authorized to share.
prompt: Review my draft as a skeptical methods reader. Pick the three claims most exposed to confounding or missing evidence. For each, name the page, explain the objection, and suggest the smallest analysis or wording change that would address it.
check: Discard critiques aimed at methods the draft already covers. Have a co-author independently assess the strongest remaining objection.
inputs: Your draft, target journal criteria and an approved private workspace
sourceLabel: Rigorous author’s peer-review demo on Hacker News

title: Test whether a model improvement survives a fair comparison
task: Turn a promising result into a small experiment that can tell whether the change helped.
prompt: In an isolated research environment, compare [change] to the supplied baseline. Hold the data split and compute budget fixed, repeat with the agreed seeds, and return the per-run scores, run log and a plot including failed runs.
check: Check the configurations differ only where planned and reproduce one run. Compare variation across seeds with the claimed improvement.
inputs: An approved research sandbox, licensed dataset, baseline and compute limit

title: Find bird calls worth listening to in a long recording
task: Turn hours of field audio into a short listening queue with timestamps and clips.
prompt: Scan these recordings from [site and date]. Group candidate calls by species and hour. Include one clear clip and one uncertain clip for each candidate, with timestamps in the original file.
check: Listen to the clips and check the spectrogram before recording a sighting. Mark calls masked by traffic or wind as uncertain.
inputs: Field recordings, approximate location and recording times

title: Turn a puzzling lesson into a one-variable experiment
task: Give learners a small interactive model they can use to test one prediction.
prompt: Use this lesson on [concept] to build an interactive demonstration. Let the learner change one quantity, predict the result and reveal the outcome beside its explanation. Add the equation, units and two worked checks.
check: Set the controls to both worked examples yourself. Confirm the model stays inside the range where the lesson’s assumptions apply.
inputs: Lesson notes, a governing rule and two instructor-verified examples
sourceLabel: Anthropic research on actual faculty use

title: Practice the question your thesis chapter cannot dodge
task: Rehearse a short oral defense that follows up when an answer outruns the evidence.
prompt: Read [chapter]. Ask me one question about the weakest assumption, wait for my answer, then challenge one part using a specific passage. After three exchanges, list what I answered and which claim still needs support.
check: Check that the cited chapter passages exist. Re-answer the hardest question aloud without the transcript and compare the two attempts.
inputs: A chapter you own, its evidence and time for a live practice round

title: Turn missed quiz questions into a second-chance lesson
task: Get fresh practice on a specific misunderstanding using the material your class actually covered.
prompt: Build a short quiz from these notes. After I answer, use each missed question to find the relevant source passage and give me a different problem testing the same concept. Keep the explanation hidden until my second attempt.
check: Match explanations to the course materials. Check that the second problem requires the same reasoning with genuinely different facts.
inputs: Your own course notes and a short practice session

title: Coach an essay revision without writing the essay
task: Give a writer one revision at a time against the assignment’s actual criteria.
prompt: Read the assignment and my draft. Find the claim with the weakest link to its evidence. Show the sentence, ask me a question about the gap, and wait for my rewrite. Recheck it against the rubric and track what improved.
check: The writer supplies every revised sentence. Compare the first and last drafts against the same single rubric criterion.
inputs: Your draft, assignment instructions and teacher’s rubric

title: Make a handwritten family diary searchable
task: Build a date and place index that opens the original scan behind every diary entry.
prompt: Work on copies of these pages I have permission to share. Transcribe each entry, link it to its scan, and build an index of people, places and dates. Mark uncertain words with a question mark and keep the original spelling beside any modern search term.
check: Read the hardest pages side by side with the transcriptions. Resolve names with a second source and review mentions of living people before sharing.
inputs: Numbered diary scans and permission to process them
sourceLabel: A family’s US Forest Service diary project on Hacker News

title: Catch real identifiers attached to the wrong paper
task: Find references that look legitimate because their DOI works but whose title or author belongs to another paper.
prompt: Resolve the identifiers in this bibliography against publisher or registry metadata. Match title, lead author and year, then give me a review sheet of discrepancies and failed lookups with the original reference intact.
check: Open the publisher record for every flagged mismatch. Separately read the cited passage to decide whether the correctly identified paper supports your claim.
inputs: A bibliography with DOIs, PubMed IDs or arXiv identifiers
sourceLabel: Scholar Sidekick author’s citation-checking test on Hacker News

title: Build a rough cut from a shelf of interview footage
task: Hand an editor a short, editable sequence with every clip linked to its original timecode.
prompt: Build a [length] sequence comparing how three interviewees answered [question]. Select a complete thought from each, put their points of agreement and disagreement in order, and add source filenames, timecodes and cutaway options to an editable timeline.
check: Play the source around each cut. An editor checks the sequence for misleading juxtapositions and signs off on picture and sound.
inputs: Cleared footage, transcripts or an approved transcription service, and an editing brief
sourceLabel: Video editor’s Claude Code rough-cut demo on Hacker News
